postTitle: Is 0% EMI or Buy Now Pay Later Really Free? When Free Is Free
topic: Free until a deadline: on some store cards, anything left unpaid brings interest back to the day of purchase

assumptions.notes: Lesson example (deferred interest): €1,200 on a store card, no interest if paid in full within a year. Paying €90 a month leaves €120 at the deadline; at 25% a year, interest charged back to the purchase date is about €176 (lesson), more than the €120 left. The reel keeps €90 and €120 in words (council Nov 5: number budget). Numbers in the reel: 0%, €1,200, €176, and 25% in the disclosure.

caption.instagram:
0% on a store card, then €176 of interest? Here is how that happens.

A €1,200 purchase, no interest if all of it is paid within a year. The monthly payments fall a little short, so at the deadline some is still unpaid. Because of that, interest is charged back to the day of purchase: about €176, more than what was left. That is called deferred interest.
